# ovis-terminal agent manual

`ovis-terminal` is the agent-facing client of the ovis-terminal runtime. It draws
nothing and never prompts. This manual ships inside the binary and describes exactly
this build; `ovis-terminal --skill --json` returns it with the version and protocol
generation it belongs to, and `ovis-terminal schema` returns the protocol of the same
version.

## Output contract

- Add `--json` (or set `OVIS_JSON=1`) for machine output. The mode never depends on
  whether stdout is a terminal: under a PTY and through a pipe the channels are the same.
- Success: one JSON document on stdout, nothing on stderr, exit 0.
- Failure: nothing on stdout, one `{"error": {...}}` object on stderr, and a non-zero
  exit code from the table below. `error.kind` is the stable token to branch on;
  `error.origin` is `cli` when this binary refused or failed, `server` when the
  runtime returned a typed error (its `data` fields are passed through); `error.hint`
  says what to do next and `error.exit_code` repeats the exit code.
- The command line is parsed and every typed parameter is checked before any socket
  is opened. A usage error exits 2 without contacting the endpoint.
- Text mode is for people. A string value is printed with its control characters
  escaped, so program text (a prompt, a screen line) can never start a line of its own
  or reach your terminal as a control sequence. Never pipe output into a shell.

## Discovery (offline, side-effect free)

- `ovis-terminal --skill` prints this manual.
- `ovis-terminal schema` prints the OpenRPC document this build speaks (same bytes as
  `schema/ovis-terminal.openrpc.json` of its source tree); `info.version` is the version
  `--skill --json` reports.
- `ovis-terminal schema cli` prints every command, flag, environment variable and exit
  code of this binary as JSON.
- `ovis-terminal schema contract` prints the runtime contract reference: every method,
  event, error kind, limit, role and exit code, generated from this build's types.
- `ovis-terminal schema compat --released <path>` checks that this build keeps every
  client of a released OpenRPC baseline working: released methods, events and required
  outputs stay, inputs only widen. A break exits 1 with `compatibility_break` and lists
  each `{path, rule}` in `breaks`; a baseline of another generation is
  `generation_mismatch`; an unreadable or non-OpenRPC file is `baseline_unreadable` or
  `baseline_malformed`. The release stage runs it on every built artifact.
- `ovis-terminal endpoint` prints the endpoint this invocation resolves to
  (`OVIS_TERMINAL_SOCKET`, `OVIS_TERMINAL_SESSION`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`,
  `HOME`, `USERNAME`) without touching it.

None of these, and no inspection command, starts, installs or restarts a server. Only
the explicit `serve` and `hold` verbs below run one, in the foreground.

## Credentials and roles

- The bearer credential is read from `OVIS_TERMINAL_CREDENTIAL` and is never printed.
  `serve` prints an owner bearer and an observe-only bearer when it starts.
- A credential grants permissions; roles bundle them. `observer` may read and subscribe,
  `interactor` may also type, resize, launch and change layout, and `owner` holds every
  permission, including takeover, prompt answers, raw input, reports and administration.
  `ovis-terminal schema contract` lists the permission every action needs.
- A program the runtime spawned finds its process token in `OVIS_TERMINAL_PROCESS_TOKEN`.
  The token proves which program owns a terminal; the verbs that report as that program
  send it automatically when `--params` names none. A token of another terminal is
  refused (`not_owner`, or `forbidden` at the prompt bridge gate; exit 12) and changes
  nothing.

## Commands that reach the endpoint

- `ovis-terminal server status` reports `running`, `stopped`, `unreachable` or
  `stale_endpoint`. A stopped server stays stopped.
- `ovis-terminal server metrics` reads stream, queue, lag and latency metrics.
- `ovis-terminal server stop --op-id ID --params '{"scope": ...}'` and
  `ovis-terminal server restart --op-id ID` are explicit mutations.
- `ovis-terminal terminal list` lists terminals.
- `ovis-terminal terminal get --terminal-id ID | --address ADDR | --name NAME` reads one
  record. Without a target it exits 7 with `needs_target` and `candidates`; it never
  picks a terminal for you. `candidates_listed` is false when no server answered.
- `ovis-terminal op new` prints a fresh operation identity (a UUIDv7 minted now) for a
  mutation's `--op-id`; it is offline and starts nothing. An id older than the server's
  operation retention window is refused as `op_expired`, so never hard-code one: write
  `--op-id "$(ovis-terminal op new)"`, and keep the id to resend the same mutation.
- `ovis-terminal op get --op-id ID` and `ovis-terminal op cancel --op-id ID` inspect or
  cancel an operation.
- `ovis-terminal call METHOD --params JSON` sends any published method except `hello`.
- `ovis-terminal connect` relays stdin and stdout to the endpoint; stdout carries
  protocol bytes only.

## Typed agent verbs

Each verb sends one published method. Its flags are exactly what that method's closed
params type takes: `--op-id ID` for a mutation, one of `--terminal-id`, `--address` or
`--name` for a terminal-scoped method, and `--params JSON` for every other field. A
field given both as a flag and in `--params` is a usage error. A terminal-scoped verb
whose other fields are valid but that names no target exits 7 with `needs_target` and
`candidates`; a malformed one exits 2 first, before any connection.

- Agents: `ovis-terminal agent register`, `ovis-terminal agent get`,
  `ovis-terminal agent update-session`, `ovis-terminal agent children`,
  `ovis-terminal agent conversation`, `ovis-terminal agent append-records`,
  `ovis-terminal agent records`, `ovis-terminal agent history`.
- Status: `ovis-terminal status get`, `ovis-terminal status report`,
  `ovis-terminal status clear`. A report with a `seq` not above the current one is
  refused with the current sequence.
- Prompts: `ovis-terminal prompt list`, `ovis-terminal prompt get`,
  `ovis-terminal prompt open`, `ovis-terminal prompt answer`, `ovis-terminal prompt close`.
- Turns: `ovis-terminal turn get`, `ovis-terminal turn wait`.
- Templates: `ovis-terminal template list`, `ovis-terminal template get`.

Every verb sends a method this build's `serve` routes; `ovis-terminal --json schema cli`
names each verb's `method`, and `hello.methods` lists what a server routes: every
published method except an explicit excluded set. `agent.list` is served without a verb;
reach it with `ovis-terminal call agent.list`. The published methods `agent.note`,
`agent.release` and `agent.wait_children` (with `doc.list`, `machine.exec`,
`machine.file`, `machine.login`, `machine.rm`, `service.install` and `service.remove`)
are excluded from this build: hello does not advertise them, and `ovis-terminal call`
with one answers `not_implemented` (exit 1) with a hint naming the follow-up.

Examples (the CLI crate's tests execute every line against `serve` of this build and
require exit 0, unless a line ends with `# exits <code> <kind>`):

```sh
ovis-terminal --json agent get --address t1
ovis-terminal --json agent register --address t1 --op-id "$(ovis-terminal op new)" --params '{"label":"my-agent","session":null}'
ovis-terminal --json status report --address t1 --op-id "$(ovis-terminal op new)" --params '{"seq":"1","record":{"state":"working"}}'
ovis-terminal --json prompt list --address t1
ovis-terminal --json turn wait --address t1 --params '{"turn":"1","timeout_ms":"1000"}'
ovis-terminal --json call agent.list --params '{}'
ovis-terminal --json call agent.note --params '{}'  # exits 1 not_implemented
```

`agent get` answers `{"agent": null, ...}` for a terminal that runs a plain program;
`not_found` means the terminal does not exist.

## Serving (Unix)

- `ovis-terminal serve [--root DIR] [--stdin-lifetime]` runs the control server in the
  foreground: endpoint, authority, stores, a shared holder and every routed method.
  With `--root` the socket is `DIR/run/s.sock` and state lives in `DIR/state`;
  otherwise the resolved endpoint is used. It prints one line
  `{"ready": {"socket", "bearer", "observer"}}` (owner and observe-only bearers) before
  serving, stops on SIGINT, SIGTERM or, with `--stdin-lifetime`, end of stdin, and then
  prints one `{"report": {...}}` line. Programs it launched end with it.
- `hello` lists exactly the methods `serve` routes; every other catalog method answers
  `method_not_found`, never a placeholder result.
- `ovis-terminal hold [--session S]` runs the session holder in the foreground, owned by
  no service manager.

## Attaching (Unix)

- `ovis-terminal terminal attach --target ADDR | --terminal-id ID | --name NAME` attaches
  this terminal: stdout carries the program's screen, the terminal is raw while
  attached, typed bytes go to the program only under the interact lease, window
  resizes are applied under the geometry lease, and Ctrl-\ detaches. Ctrl-C goes to
  the program. It needs a TTY on stdin and stdout (`not_a_tty`, exit 2, otherwise).
- There is no prefix key and no client mode: every byte other than Ctrl-\, unknown
  escape sequences and non-UTF-8 bytes included, reaches the program unchanged through
  `input.raw`, or the server's typed refusal ends the attach.
- Another holder is never displaced: a held lease exits 11 with `lease_conflict`, the
  holder's lease record in `holder` and the lease change to retry after in `retry`.
- The lease belongs to the connection that acquired it and is recorded under
  `--client-id`, which defaults to `cli-<pid>`. A second attach is always another owner,
  even under the same `--client-id`: it exits 11 with `lease_conflict` and cannot type.
- `--takeover EPOCH` displaces the interact holder only at its current epoch and with
  the takeover grant; a stale epoch exits 11 with `lease_epoch_mismatch`, the epoch
  sent in `expected_epoch` and the current lease in `current`.
- `--observe` needs no TTY, never reads stdin, never writes input and never resizes;
  on a terminal, Ctrl-\ (SIGQUIT) detaches it.
- The outcome record goes to stderr: `{"detached": {"reason", "stream_closed",
  "leases_released", "leases_held", "displaced", ...}}` (exit 0) for Ctrl-\, a hung-up
  terminal, SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGQUIT, or the error record for a refusal; a
  signal before the stream is attached exits 10 with `interrupted` and its `stage`; a
  lost connection exits 4 with `connection_lost`. The outer terminal's settings, and
  the modes the program switched on (alternate screen, mouse, bracketed paste, cursor
  keys, keyboard protocol, hidden cursor), are restored on every one of these.

## Holder service (Unix)

The session holder owns every PTY and outlives the command that started it. Only
`status` is read-only; every other verb is an explicit mutation and names its manager.

- `ovis-terminal service status [--session S]` reports `running`, `stopped`,
  `unreachable` or `stale_endpoint` from the discovery record, the recorded process's
  start token and one connection attempt. It never starts, installs or repairs anything,
  and lists `missing_prerequisites` for surviving a logout.
- `ovis-terminal service install --manager systemd-user|launchd` writes and loads the
  service definition; `ovis-terminal service uninstall --manager ...` removes only a
  definition this runtime wrote, after the holder stopped.
- `ovis-terminal service start --manager systemd-user|launchd|detached` starts the
  holder. `detached` puts it in its own session with no manager: it survives the
  starting command and its terminal, but not a logout that ends every user process.
- `ovis-terminal service stop` stops the holder and lists the holder process and every
  terminal and process it ended. A stale endpoint is reported, not cleaned; the next
  `service start` replaces an endpoint whose process is proven gone.
- `ovis-terminal service run` is the holder process itself, executed by the manager or
  by `start`; do not run it by hand.

## Exit codes

| code | name | kinds |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | success | |
| 1 | failure | any kind not listed below |
| 2 | usage | usage, invalid_params, unknown_method, invalid_json_switch, not_a_tty, endpoint and service path configuration kinds |
| 3 | not_found | not_found, template_not_found, parent_not_found, stream_not_found, not_registered |
| 4 | unavailable | unavailable, server_not_running, stale_endpoint, method_not_found, machine_unreachable, unsupported_transport, backpressure, recovering, not_ready, service_manager_unavailable, service_unsupported, connection_lost |
| 7 | needs_target | needs_target, ambiguous_target |
| 9 | blocked | blocked |
| 10 | cancelled | cancelled, interrupted |
| 11 | conflict | conflict and state conflicts such as op_reused, already_running, lease_conflict or lease_epoch_mismatch |
| 12 | forbidden | forbidden, unauthenticated, not_owner, credential kinds and attach_refused |
| 13 | outcome_unknown | outcome_unknown, deadline_exceeded, manager_timeout, holder_not_ready: inspect the operation or the service status |

`ovis-terminal schema cli` lists the exact kinds of each code, and
`ovis-terminal schema contract` lists every server error kind with its recovery.

# ovis-terminal runtime contract

Reference for `ovis-terminal 0.1.0`, protocol generation 1. Generated by `ovis-terminal schema contract` from the types of that build; do not edit it by hand.

## How to read this reference

The tables from `## Methods` on are rendered from the Rust types of this build: the OpenRPC
document, the authorization roles and the exit codes. They are the same on every platform;
the platform's commands are in the manual and `ovis-terminal schema cli`. The sections
before them state behaviour that types cannot express. They come from the runtime API
advisory with the binding decisions of the work plan applied; `## Advisory overrides
applied` lists every place where the plan replaced the advisory.

## Transport and framing

- A connection is persistent and multiplexed: requests are matched by string `id`, many
  may be in flight, and the server never closes after a reply. A server-initiated close
  sends `$/closing{reason}` first when the socket is writable.
- Plain mode is UTF-8 JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per `\n`-terminated line, no batches.
  Fragmentation never defines a message.
- After a successful `hello` a connection can upgrade to framed mode at an explicit parser
  boundary. Every frame has a nine-byte header `[channel:u32 LE][kind:u8][len:u32 LE]`.
  Channel 0 carries JSON-RPC; DATA on a nonzero channel is downstream terminal data;
  CREDIT carries an eight-byte little-endian cumulative acknowledged delivery offset of
  that never-reused channel and stream; CLOSE is typed control. Oversize, truncated and
  unknown frames are typed errors, never ignored.
- Input, resize, focus and takeover are RPCs (`input.*`, `attach.resize`, `attach.focus`,
  `attach.takeover`), never anonymous writes on a stream.
- Every u64 counter, sequence, revision, offset and generation is a canonical decimal
  string on the wire. A JSON number in its place is `invalid_params`.
- Raw holder output offsets and filtered stream delivery offsets are separate domains.
  Attach control records bind both; CREDIT acknowledges only delivery offsets.

## Identity and targeting

- Identities are distinct types and never conflated: `machine_id`, `runtime_lifetime`,
  `server_boot_id`, `terminal_id`, terminal and process incarnations (a process
  incarnation carries `pid` and a platform start token), `stream_id`, `lease_id` and
  `lease_epoch`, `op_id`, `prompt_id`, `agent_id`.
- A `target` is exactly one of `{terminal_id}`, `{address}` (`t7`, `machine/t7`) or
  `{name}`. Params are closed objects: an unknown or misspelled field is `invalid_params`
  with its `field_path`, and nothing runs. There is no focus and no focus fallback.
- A name that resolves to several terminals is `ambiguous_target` with candidates; a
  command-line read without a target is `needs_target` with candidates, never a guess.

## Operations, idempotency and outcomes

- Every mutation takes a client-minted `op_id`. Resending the same `op_id` with the same
  params returns the retained result; different params are `op_reused`.
- State rows, the operation receipt and its events commit in one transaction, and the
  result is published only after the commit.
- `op.get` distinguishes accepted, running, committed, failed, cancelled and
  outcome-unknown, with supporting receipts or process evidence. A mutation whose
  connection was lost is never resent automatically; ask `op.get` first.
- Admission and later effects are separate facts: `input.send` returns an admission
  receipt with an output cursor and never waits for a status transition; `turn.wait`,
  `terminal.wait_output` and `events.wait` are separate, bounded calls. A cursor older
  than the retained floor answers `gap`, not `timeout`.
- `input.interrupt` reports delivery and observed process or agent state as separate
  fields; stopped is true only with exit evidence or a declared report that left
  `working`.

## Terminal lifecycle states

| from | trigger | to |
|---|---|---|
| none | `terminal.run` committed | `live` with spawn pending |
| `live` (pending) | holder reports pid and start token | `live` |
| `live` (pending) | spawn failure, not kept | `finished` (`spawn_failed`) |
| `live` | program exit or `terminal.kill` observed | `finished` (`exited`, `killed` or `signaled`) |
| `live` | loss while kept | `lost` |
| `lost` | grace elapsed or `terminal.recover` | `restarting` |
| `restarting` | program spawned | `live` with new incarnations |
| `lost` or `restarting` | `terminal.keep` false | `finished` |
| any live state | host reboot detected | `finished` (`host_shutdown`) as restored metadata |
| `finished` | `terminal.rm` or retention | removed, with a tombstone |

Waits end on `lost` as they do on `finished`. A planned control restart changes
`server_boot_id` but not `runtime_lifetime` while holders survive; a reboot starts a new
lifetime and reports restored metadata, never live processes.

## Leases, attach and input ordering

| state | event | next |
|---|---|---|
| no interact lease | `attach.open` interact | held by the opener, who owns geometry |
| any | `attach.open` observe | unchanged; the observer never writes |
| held by A | interact open by B without takeover | held by A; B is told who holds it |
| held by A | `attach.takeover` by B with the takeover grant and A's current epoch | held by B; A's stream closes as taken over |
| held by A | takeover at a stale epoch | held by A; `lease_epoch_mismatch` names the current lease |
| held by A | A closes or disconnects | no lease; geometry owner cleared |
| any | terminal `lost` or `finished` | no lease |

- The epoch advances on every interact transition. Only an explicit, authorized takeover
  displaces a holder.
- No human-controller bypass is implicit: whenever any lease exists, writes require the
  current interact lease, and lease-free agent writes require an explicitly granted
  input scope. DATA from an observer is rejected immediately.
- One terminal actor serializes admission. Input authority, target, process and lease
  identity and the mode revision are checked at admission and again at the actual write
  boundary; takeover or revocation fences entries not yet written and never claims to
  retract bytes already written.
- Terminal-query replies use a separate bounded internal lane and can never become user
  submissions.

## Agent status, prompts and turns

| current root | input | next root | turn |
|---|---|---|---|
| unreported | report with a higher `seq` | the reported state | unchanged |
| `working` | report `idle`, `done`, `error` or `blocked` | that state | ends, +1 |
| not `working` | report `working` | `working` | unchanged |
| any | report with `seq` not above the current one | unchanged; the report is refused with the current sequence | unchanged |
| any | `status.clear` by the owner | cleared | unchanged |
| `working` | process exit | cleared | ends as `exited` |

- Status has exactly two writers: OSC 7501 bytes from the owning program's PTY and
  `status.report` presented with that program's process token. An accepted report stands
  until replaced, cleared or invalidated by its declared lifetime; screen text, process
  names and brands are never status.
- A process token belongs to one process incarnation of one terminal. A report, prompt,
  record or registration that presents another terminal's token is refused and changes
  nothing.
- `agent.register` accepts any label and session reference. `agent.get` on a plain
  program returns `agent: null`; `not_found` is reserved for a missing terminal.
- Prompts are versioned records. `prompt.answer` names the prompt and its version and
  needs the prompt-answer grant; a second answer to the same version is a conflict.
- Provider-store adapters produce conversation records only and never lifecycle status.
  A first message is released only on declared readiness, never on output silence.

## Events, snapshots and replay

- Every event has one envelope with sequence, lifetime, boot, machine, type, target and
  typed data. Snapshots and events share one sequence domain per runtime lifetime.
- A subscription starts with a snapshot at a revision followed only by matching changes
  committed after it. Several subscriptions on one connection are independent; filter
  changes are acknowledged with an effective sequence.
- Reconnecting with a retained cursor replays later matching events; otherwise the
  answer is `missed` with a fresh snapshot. A cursor from another lifetime is never
  replayed.
- Snapshot pagination pins one revision across pages.

## Persistence and recovery

- One SQLite database in WAL mode holds terminals, receipts, events, status, prompts,
  agents and documents; each mutation is one transaction.
- Holders own PTYs and raw retained output; the control core owns VT checkpoints,
  layout, leases, operation state and domain events. One shared holder serves a session
  and build; a planned control restart keeps every program incarnation.
- At start the core recovers holders and checkpoints and reports recovery boundaries.
  Recovery evidence persists across reads: neither `server.status` nor `server.metrics`
  clears it. An unsupported or damaged database is preserved, not overwritten.

## Concurrency and bounds

- Each terminal has one serialized actor and bounded message channels; blocking PTY and
  SQLite work runs off the async executor; every task is cancellable and joined.
- Every mailbox, queue, retention window and allocation is bounded and advertised in
  `hello` (see `## Limits`). Limits are admission budgets, not preallocations; a full
  queue answers `backpressure`, never a silent drop.
- A slow consumer of one stream gets a gap and a fresh checkpoint instead of an unbounded
  backlog; other streams and channel 0 are unaffected.

## Edge cases

- Input to a `lost` or `restarting` terminal is refused as `recovering`; nothing is
  queued and nothing is replayed later.
- `attach.open` on a finished terminal delivers the final checkpoint and then closes.
- A frame larger than the frame limit closes the connection after `$/closing`; its
  streams close and its leases are revoked as on disconnect.
- PID reuse is detected by the process start token; a mismatched incarnation is refused.
- A UTF-8 code point split across PTY reads is decoded correctly on the screen and passed
  unchanged on streams.
- A malformed or oversized OSC 7501 sequence changes no status.
- Duplicate live names are refused; a name that looks like an address is invalid.
- A control-server crash during a send leaves the operation `outcome_unknown` until
  `op.get` shows its evidence; the client must not resend blindly.
- A program that never declares readiness keeps its first message held until the
  deadline, then the message expires; the screen is untouched.
- A document over the size limit is refused with its version unchanged.

## Excluded behaviours

- EXCL-001: the runtime draws no sidebar, onboarding or modal chrome; nothing presentational gates a headless operation.
- EXCL-002: no prefix key and no client mode; no byte is swallowed by an invisible mode.
- EXCL-003: every operation has a typed, discoverable equivalent; nothing depends on a pointer target.
- EXCL-004: an RPC never promotes a client to the foreground or takes geometry authority.
- EXCL-005 and EXCL-006: explicit targets only; a wrong or unknown field is an error, never an answer about another terminal.
- EXCL-007: only an explicit, authorized takeover at the current epoch displaces a controller.
- EXCL-008 and EXCL-009: no screen-tail status, no brand detection, no downloaded detection manifests.
- EXCL-010: a declared agent of any label is queryable; a plain program has `agent: null`.
- EXCL-011, EXCL-012 and EXCL-013: no toasts, sounds or announcement modals; clients decide how to notify from durable events.
- EXCL-014 and EXCL-015: persistent multiplexed connections; independent, acknowledged subscriptions.
- EXCL-016: attach refusals and handoffs are typed outcomes, never terminal text.
- EXCL-017: unknown input sequences travel as raw bytes or fail with a typed error; nothing is discarded silently.
- EXCL-018: destructive scope is visible in help, schema, validation and receipts.
- EXCL-019: reads never inject input or scroll the program they inspect.
- EXCL-020 and EXCL-021: every managed invocation has an operation identity, bounded output and an exit outcome; failures stay queryable.
- EXCL-022: split and pane identities are stable node ids, never tree paths.
- EXCL-023: no force-send; a blocked program is reached through a versioned prompt answer or explicit raw interaction.
- EXCL-024, EXCL-025 and EXCL-026: admission, delivery, output waits and interrupt evidence are separate facts.
- EXCL-027: read-only status, schema, manual and help never start, install or restart a server.

## Advisory overrides applied

- Stack: the advisory's Bun runtime with one holder process per terminal is replaced by a Rust runtime with one shared holder per session and build (plan, Must have).
- Resource model: the advisory's terminals-only model is overruled; a thin deterministic workspace, tab, pane and split layout service exists in the core (plan, Execution strategy; IDEAL-084 to IDEAL-088).
- Frame kinds: the advisory's RESIZE, FOCUS and FACTS frames are replaced by RPCs; framed connections carry DATA, CREDIT and CLOSE only (plan, Settled contracts).

- Observer writes: the advisory's warn-then-close rule is replaced by immediate rejection of observer DATA (plan, Steering and complete-spec reconciliation).

- Numbers: every u64 value travels as a canonical decimal string (plan, Settled contracts).
- Discovery: `ovis-terminal endpoint` describes the resolved endpoint without probing it; liveness is `server status`, which never starts anything (plan, IDEAL-014 and IDEAL-111).

## Roles and permissions

A credential grants permissions; a role is a named bundle. No permission implies another, and only the owner role bundles takeover, prompt answers and raw input. A program's process token is not a credential: it proves which program owns a terminal when that program reports status, prompts or records, and a token of another terminal is refused.

|---|---|
| observer | observe |
| interactor | observe, interact |
| owner | observe, interact, raw_input, takeover, prompt_answer, report, admin, plugin |

## Command line

`--json` (or `OVIS_JSON=1`) selects JSON whatever stdout is: a result is one JSON document on stdout, a failure is one `{"error": {...}}` record on stderr with `origin` (`cli` or `server`), `kind`, `hint` and `exit_code`. The command line is parsed and typed before any connection.
